42730-stand-fast-craig-royston-volume-ii.title: A Novel
42730-stand-fast-craig-royston-volume-ii.creator: Unknown
42730-stand-fast-craig-royston-volume-ii.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. had witnessed Maisrie's devotion to her grandfather, her gentle forbearance and consideration, her skilful humouring of him, and her never-failing faith in him, must have got to know what kind of man was old George Bethune.

arxiv-1806-09327.title: Linear Representations and Frobenius Morphisms of Groupoids
arxiv-1806-09327.creator: Juan Jesús BARBARÁN SÁNCHEZ † and Laiachi EL KAOUTIT ‡
arxiv-1806-09327.description: Abstract Given a morphism of (small) groupoids with injective object map, we provide sufficient and necessary conditions under which the induction and co-induction functors between the categories of linear representations are naturally isomorphic. A morphism with this property is termed a Frobenius morphism of groupoids .

arxiv-2110-04242.title: Surface Quasigeostrophic Turbulence in Variable Stratification
arxiv-2110-04242.description: Abstract Numerical and observational evidence indicates that, in regions where mixed-layer instability is active, the surface geostrophic velocity is largely induced by surface buoyancy anomalies. Yet, in these regions, the observed surface kinetic energy spectrum is steeper than predicted by uniformly stratified surface quasigeostrophic theory.

arxiv-2110-12476.title: On A α A_{\alpha} -spectrum of joined union of graphs and its applications to power graphs of finite groups
arxiv-2110-12476.creator: Bilal A. Rather, Hilal A. Ganie, S. Pirzada
arxiv-2110-12476.description: Abstract Abstract. For a simple graph G , the generalized adjacency matrix A_{\alpha}(G) is defined as A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G),\alpha\in[0,1] , where A(G) is the adjacency matrix and D(G) is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees of G . This matrix generalises the spectral theories of the adjacency matrix and the signless Laplacian matrix of G .

arxiv-2211-13576.title: Why and When to Expect Gaussian Error Distributions in Epoch of Reionization 21-cm Power Spectrum Measurements
arxiv-2211-13576.creator: Michael J. Wilensky, Jordan Brown, Bryna J. Hazelton
arxiv-2211-13576.description: Abstract We explore error distributions in Epoch of Reionization 21-cm power spectrum estimators using a combination of mathematical analysis and numerical simulations. We provide closed form solutions for the error distributions of individual bins in 3d-power spectra for two estimators currently in use in the field, which we designate as “straight-square” and “cross-multiply” estimators.

arxiv-2212-09859.title: CompuMat: A Computational Composite Material for Tangible Interaction Conference: TEI ’23: Proceedings of the Seventeenth International Conference on Tangible, Embedded, and Embodied Interaction; February 26-March 1, 2023; Warsaw, Poland TEI ’23: Proceedings of the Seventeenth International Conferen
arxiv-2212-09859.creator: Xinyi Yang, Martin Nisser, Stefanie Mueller
arxiv-2212-09859.description: Abstract . This paper introduces a computational composite material comprising layers for actuation, computation and energy storage. Key to its design is inexpensive materials assembled from traditionally available fabrication machines to support the rapid exploration of applications from computational composites.

arxiv-2402-04808.title: Basis expansion approaches for Functional Analysis of Variance with repeated measures Journal: Advances in Data Analysis and Classification
arxiv-2402-04808.creator: Christian Acal, Ana M. Aguilera
arxiv-2402-04808.description: Abstract The methodological contribution in this paper is motivated by biomechanical studies where data characterizing human movement are waveform curves representing joint measures such as flexion angles, velocity, acceleration, and so on. In many cases the aim consists of detecting differences in gait patterns when several independent samples of subjects walk or run under different conditions (repeated measures).

arxiv-2403-03938.title: GUIDE: Guidance-based Incremental Learning with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2403-03938.creator: Bartosz Cywiński, Kamil Deja, Tomasz Trzciński, Bartłomiej Twardowski, Łukasz Kuciński
arxiv-2403-03938.description: Abstract We introduce GUIDE, a novel continual learning approach that directs diffusion models to rehearse samples at risk of being forgotten. Existing generative strategies combat catastrophic forgetting by randomly sampling rehearsal examples from a generative model. Such an approach contradicts buffer-based approaches where sampling strategy plays an important role.

arxiv-2404-10924.title: Binder : Hierarchical Concept Representation through Order Embedding of Binary Vectors
arxiv-2404-10924.creator: Croix Gyurek, Niloy Talukder, Mohammad Al Hasan
arxiv-2404-10924.description: Abstract . For natural language understanding and generation, embedding concepts using an order-based representation is an essential task. Unlike traditional point vector based representation, an order-based representation imposes geometric constraints on the representation vectors for explicitly capturing various semantic relationships that may exist between a pair of concepts.

arxiv-2407-07596.title: Learning treatment effects while treating those in need
arxiv-2407-07596.creator: Bryan Wilder, Pim Welle
arxiv-2407-07596.description: Abstract . Many social programs attempt to allocate scarce resources to people with the greatest need. Indeed, public services increasingly use algorithmic risk assessments motivated by this goal. However, targeting the highest-need recipients often conflicts with attempting to evaluate the causal effect of the program as a whole, as the best evaluations would be obtained by randomizing the allocation.

arxiv-2410-17399.title: An Anatomy of Event Studies: Hypothetical Experiments, Exact Decomposition, and Weighting Diagnostics Thanks: The authors thank Dmitry Arkhangelsky, Francesca Dominici, Avi Feller, Phillip Heiler, Miguel Hernán, Guido Imbens, Andrea Rotnitzky, Pedro Sant’Anna, Zach Shahn, Tymon Słoczyński, Dylan Sma
arxiv-2410-17399.creator: Zhu Shen, Ambarish Chattopadhyay, Yuzhou Lin, José R. Zubizarreta
arxiv-2410-17399.description: Abstract In recent decades, event studies have become widely used in health and social research to estimate the dynamic effects of staggered interventions. In this paper, we develop a framework grounded in experimental design principles for observational studies that encompasses common event study estimators and makes explicit how they borrow information across units and time periods.

arxiv-2502-18398.title: Perturbative solutions for compact objects in (2+1)-dimensional Bopp-Podolsky electrodynamics
arxiv-2502-18398.creator: R. V. Maluf, J. E. G. Silva, C. A. S. Almeida, Gonzalo J. Olmo
arxiv-2502-18398.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by R. V. Maluf, J. E. G. Silva, C. A. S. Almeida, Gonzalo J. Olmo. We investigate the space-time geometry generated by compact objects in (2+1)-dimensional Bopp-Podolsky electrodynamics. Inspired by previous studies where the Bopp-Podolsky field acts as a source for spherically symmetric solutions, we revisit this question within the lower-dimensional (2+1) framework. Using a perturbative approach, we derive a charged BTZ-like black hole solution and compute corrections up to second order in a perturbative expansion valid far from the horizon.

arxiv-2601-15814.title: Improved Approximation Ratios for the Shortest Common Superstring Problem with Reverse Complements
arxiv-2601-15814.creator: Ryosuke Yamano, Tetsuo Shibuya
arxiv-2601-15814.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ryosuke Yamano, Tetsuo Shibuya. The Shortest Common Superstring (SCS) problem asks for the shortest string that contains each of a given set of strings as a substring. Its reverse-complement variant, the Shortest Common Superstring problem with Reverse Complements (SCS-RC), naturally arises in bioinformatics applications, where for each input string, either the string itself or its reverse complement must appear as a substring of the superstring.

doe-osti-17028735-managed-charging-dispa.title: Managed Charging Dispatch Mechanisms: Trade-Offs and Opportunities
doe-osti-17028735-managed-charging-dispa.creator: Hale, Elaine, Lavin, Luke, Smart, John
doe-osti-17028735-managed-charging-dispa.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. Electric vehicle (EV) charging can be managed directly by an aggregator in coordination with supply-side dispatch, or it can be scheduled in response to prices. A previous production cost modeling study found that price-responsive mechanisms like time-of-use rates (TOU) and real-

macauliffe-sikh-religion-vol3-1909.creator: Max Arthur Macauliffe
macauliffe-sikh-religion-vol3-1909.description: Volume III of the first complete English account of Sikhism, with translations from the Sikh scriptures — Guru Arjan and the compilation of the Granth.

pmc-10670847.title: Evaluation of the Effect of Honey-Containing Chitosan/Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels on Wound Healing
pmc-10670847.creator: Emine Şalva, Ahmet Enes Akdağ, Saadet Alan, Sema Arısoy, Fatma Jülide Akbuğa
pmc-10670847.description: The 3D polymeric network structure of hydrogels imitates the extracellular matrix, thereby facilitating cell growth and differentiation. In the current study, chitosan/hyaluronic acid/honey coacervate hydrogels were produced without any chemicals or crosslinking agents and investigated for their wound-healing abilities. Chitosan/hyaluronic acid/honey hydrogels were characterized by FTIR, SEM, and rheology analysis.

pmc-10708766.title: RepECN: Making ConvNets Better Again for Efficient Image Super-Resolution
pmc-10708766.creator: Qiangpu Chen, Jinghui Qin, Wushao Wen, Antonio Fernández-Caballero, Byung-Gyu Kim
pmc-10708766.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Traditional Convolutional Neural Network (ConvNet, CNN)-based image super-resolution (SR) methods have lower computation costs, making them more friendly for real-world scenarios. However, they suffer from lower performance. On the contrary, Vision Transformer (ViT)-based SR methods have achieved impressive performance recently, but these methods often suffer from high computation costs and model storage overhead, making them hard to meet the requirements in practical application scenarios. In practical scenarios, an SR model should reconstruct an image with high quality and fast inference.

pmc-11396672.title: Agents Targeting the Bacterial Cell Wall as Tools to Combat Gram-Positive Pathogens
pmc-11396672.creator: Aliaksandr Zhydzetski, Zuzanna Głowacka-Grzyb, Michal Bukowski, Tomasz Żądło, Emilia Bonar, Benedykt Władyka, Marilisa Leone, Marian Vincenzi
pmc-11396672.description: The cell wall is an indispensable element of bacterial cells and a long-known target of many antibiotics. Penicillin, the first discovered beta-lactam antibiotic inhibiting the synthesis of cell walls, was successfully used to cure many bacterial infections. Unfortunately, pathogens eventually developed resistance to it.

pmc-11477359.title: Preparation and Photodegradation of TiO2 Thin Films on the Inner Wall of Quartz Tubes
pmc-11477359.creator: Wei Chen, Qi Yan, Junjiao Yang
pmc-11477359.description: Titanium dioxide thin films on the inner wall of quartz tubes were prepared in situ by the sol–gel method. Meanwhile, copper and cerium were loaded onto the surface of the titanium dioxide thin films to enhance photocatalytic activity and broaden the range of light absorption.

pmc-11517578.title: Alcohol consumption and risky sexual behaviours: consistent patterns in France and South Korea
pmc-11517578.creator: J Jeong, L Simmat-Durand
pmc-11517578.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundDespite the concurrent increase in harmful alcohol use and risky sexual behaviours associated with STIs and HIV/AIDS among young adults, their relationship remains inconsistent due to the inherent influence of sociodemographic and cultural factors on drinking and sexual practices.

pmc-11607871.title: Revealing disparities in representation in knowledge generation and guideline development
pmc-11607871.creator: Carlos P B Almeida, Afom T Andom, Alain Casseus, Jacquelyn-My Do, Alain Gelin, Leonid Lecca, Maxo Luma, Michael Mazzi, Carole D Mitnick, Jean Claude Mugunga, Melino Ndayizigiye, Natalie Nguyen, Meseret Tamirat, Girum Tefera, Sterman Toussaint, Marco Tovar, Christine Tzelios
pmc-11607871.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMultidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) is a major global health challenge, disproportionately affecting low- and lower-middle-income countries (LLMICs). The World Health Organization (WHO) generates guidance to address the problem. Here, we explore the extent to which guidance and related knowledge are generated by experts living in the most-affected countries and consider the results in the context of the movement to decolonize global health.MethodsWe examined the composition of World Health Organization (WHO) MDR/RR-TB treatment Guideline Development Groups (GDGs) from 2016 to 2022.

pmc-11640669.title: Curcumin Inhibits Oxidative Stress and Apoptosis Induced by H2O2 in Bovine Adipose-Derived Stem Cells (bADSCs)
pmc-11640669.creator: Enhui Jiang, Xuanbo Chen, Yi Bi, Chuanying Pan, Xiangchen Li, Xianyong Lan, Ioanna-Katerina Aggeli
pmc-11640669.description: Simple SummaryIn livestock farming, oxidative stress is common and hurts animal growth and product quality. Curcumin, a natural compound, can help fight oxidative stress and cell death. This study used cells from cow fat to create an oxidative stress model and tested curcumin’s effects.

pmc-12535090.title: Prevalence of transfusion-transmissible infections among blood donors in a tertiary health institution in South-west, Nigeria: a three-year retrospective study
pmc-12535090.creator: Busira Adesina Tijani, Yusuf Oluwapelumi Adedeji, Musa Abidemi Muhibi, Olufemi Olamakinwa Ala, Abdul-Afeez Abimbola Adedeji, Saidat Funke Lawal, Olamide Yetunde Aborisade, Grace Omotola Ogunwole, Olayinka Olaolu Olaniyan, Jesutofunmi Abosede Taiwo, Bashiru Shola Oseni
pmc-12535090.description: BackgroundBlood transfusion is a vital medical procedure used to treat patients with complications such as severe blood loss, blood disorders, cancers, and those undergoing surgery or experiencing obstetric emergencies. Transfusion transmissible infections (TTIs) pose a significant threat to blood transfusion safety. The prevalence of these infections among blood donors varies widely across regions.

pmc-12540920.title: Refractory Spontaneous Pneumothorax in Interstitial Lung Disease Under Pirfenidone Treatment
pmc-12540920.creator: Jaejun Jeong, Min Kyun Kang
pmc-12540920.description: Recurrent pneumothorax associated with interstitial lung disease occurs frequently. In the case of refractory pneumothorax, other methods such as mechanical pleurodesis, in addition to chemical pleurodesis, should be considered, because antifibrotics such as pirfenidone might affect the effectiveness of pleurodesis.

pmc-12608446.title: Rational Design of Amino Acid-Modified Halide Perovskites for Highly Efficient and Cost-Effective Light-Emitting Diodes
pmc-12608446.creator: Hongyu Chen, Mingxia Qiu, Roberto Macaluso
pmc-12608446.description: Formamidinium lead bromide (FAPbBr3) quantum dots (QDs) have shown potential in light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, their performance is constrained by surface defects and the limitations of charge transport. Zwitterionic ligands, owing to their twin functions of Lewis base coordination and electrostatic compensation, passivate surface defects of perovskite QDs.

pmc-12677606.title: Performance Degradation in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Under Large Load Variation at Rapid Startup: Phenomena and Solution Based on Different Flow Fields
pmc-12677606.creator: Yadong Wang, Fengyang Cai, Zhengkai Tu, Siew Hwa Chan
pmc-12677606.description: The durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) under large load variation at rapid startup is critical for commercialization. Experimental and numerical results indicate that the five‐channel serpentine flow field (FSFF) design exhibited the optimal large load variation capability at rapid startup and more effective performance degradation mitigation.

pmc-12785961.title: Influence of Peptide-Rich Nitrogen Sources on GAD System Activation and GABA Production in Levilactobacillus brevis CRL 2013
pmc-12785961.creator: María Paulina Urquiza Martínez, Pablo G. Cataldo, Natalia Soledad Ríos Colombo, Pasquale Ferranti, Lucila Saavedra, Elvira M. Hebert
pmc-12785961.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) is a bioactive metabolite valued in functional foods, but its microbial production is strongly influenced by nutrient availability. Levilactobacillus brevis CRL 2013 is an efficient GABA producer; however, its biosynthesis depends on culture medium composition. In this study, integrated physiological, proteomic, and transcriptional analyses were applied to assess the influence of nitrogen source composition and concentration on GABA production.

pmc-12991702.title: Altered Bone Geometry and Quality in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Insights from Peripheral Quantitative Computed Tomography in an Indian Cohort
pmc-12991702.creator: Anuradha V. Khadilkar, Uma Divate, Vishwajit Satale, Satyajit S. Gill, Shrikanth Muralidharan
pmc-12991702.description: Background:Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for skeletal fragility, independent of bone mineral density (BMD).Objective:This prospective, cross-sectional case-control study investigated bone geometry using peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) in 100 patients with T2DM.Methodology:100 cases of Type 2 DM and healthy cohorts were compared for bone geometry at a tertiary care hospital.

pmc-13189045.title: Salvage open partial horizontal laryngectomy: a comprehensive systematic review of oncological and functional outcomes
pmc-13189045.creator: Andy Bertolin, Alberto Grassetto, Marco Lionello, Giuseppe Rizzotto, Vincenzo della Peruta, Luigi D’Avino, Marco de Vincentiis, Giovanni Succo, Giuseppe Tortoriello
pmc-13189045.description: SummaryObjectiveTo evaluate the oncological and functional outcomes of salvage open partial horizontal laryngectomy (OPHL) following failure of transoral laser microsurgery (TOLMS) (chemo)radiotherapy [(C)RT].MethodsA comprehensive systematic review was conducted, analysing survival rates (overall survival [OS], disease-specific survival [DSS], and local control [LC]), laryngeal preservation, and functional recovery (decannulation and swallowing) in the salvage setting.

Smibert in 1984 and correspond with organisms that cause syphilis (subsp. pallidum), yaws (subsp. pertenue) and bejel (subsp. endemicum) in humans.

pmc-13578427.creator: Ronak Majid, Jajati Keshari Nayak, Sofora Jan, Sadaf Salam, Amir Nazir, Mohd Anwar Khan, Neeraj Pal, Raju Ratan Yadav, Santvana Tyagi, Pooja Joshi, Narendra Singh Dhaka, Vinay Kumar Singh, Parvaze Ahmad Sofi, Sundip Kumar, Manish K Vishwakarma, Pradeep Bhati, Uttam Kumar, Rajeev Kumar Varshney, Reyazul Rouf Mir

pmc-13621248.title: R2Tg retrotransposon mediated targeted integration of exogenous genes into the 28S rDNA locus in mammalian cell lines for PKU gene therapy
pmc-13621248.creator: Xiuyuan Wang, Ziqi Wen, Rongjun Xu, Wenjing Shi, Yiling Long, Xingri Zhan, Rui Su, Jia Fei, Yumin Li
pmc-13621248.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Phenylketonuria (PKU) remains a challenging genetic disorder due to the absence of therapeutic strategies capable of achieving sustained restoration of phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) function. Here, we employed an R2 retrotransposon in Taeniopygia guttata (R2Tg)-based system to enable targeted integration of exogenous PAH mRNA into the 28S ribosomal DNA (rDNA) locus of the host genome, with the goal of rescuing PAH deficiency caused by loss-of-function mutations.

pmc-13672936.title: Intersectionality, #MeToo, and the Mainstream Media: The New York Times’ Problematic Framing of the Blasey Ford/Kavanaugh and Reade/Biden Sexual Assault Allegations
pmc-13672936.creator: Alvaro Oleart, Noah Anton Schmitt
pmc-13672936.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This article asks: How did The New York Times’ opinion section frame the sexual assault allegations of Christine Blasey Ford against Brett Kavanaugh compared to Tara Reade's against Joe Biden? Through a framing analysis, it compares The New York Times' opinion coverage of Blasey Ford's allegations in 2018 with Reade's allegations in 2020, both of which took place in the context of the #MeToo movement.
